title: India Ordered 1,794 Sabudana Dishes an Hour During Navratri Weekend, Swiggy Says
excerpt: Sabudana khichdi and vada topped vrat orders on October 17-18, while rasgulla led a 36.4 percent rise in traditional sweet orders, according to Swiggy's festive report.
body:
• Swiggy delivered an average of 1,794 sabudana dishes an hour across India during the Navratri weekend of October 17-18, with sabudana khichdi and sabudana vada the clear favourites.
  • Orders for traditional sweets rose 36.4 percent between October 17 and 20 compared with a similar festive period last year; rasgulla led at an average of 495 orders an hour.
  • Vrat thalis — especially the Navratri Special Vrat Thali with singhara poori — drove complete-meal orders in Delhi, Bengaluru, Gurugram and Noida, including one Rs 11,072 order for 13 thalis in Noida.
  • For diaspora readers recreating a Navratri vrat plate abroad, the pattern is simple: sabudana khichdi or vada, plus singhara, kuttu, rajgira and makhana dishes, were India's most-ordered fasting foods.

India ordered sabudana at a rate few fasting foods can match this Navratri. Swiggy delivered an average of 1,794 sabudana dishes an hour across the country during the weekend of October 17-18, according to the platform's festive report covered by The Hindu BusinessLine. Sabudana khichdi and sabudana vada emerged as the favourites.

The figures cover the period from October 17 to 20, when Navratri and Durga Puja celebrations culminated in Durga Ashtami, Maha Navami and Dussehra, Storyboard18 reported.

Khichdi cities and thali orders

Demand for sabudana khichdi was strongest in Mumbai and Bengaluru, with Pune and Jaipur also ordering heavily. Other fasting favourites followed behind sabudana: Navratri vrat thalis, singhara-based preparations, kuttu and rajgira specialties, samak rice and makhana dishes.

Complete festive meals sold as curated thalis. The Navratri Special Vrat Thali with singhara poori led that category, alongside rajgira poori and aloo hing three-course thalis. Delhi, Bengaluru, Gurugram and Noida drove the highest thali demand. In Noida, one customer ordered 13 of the singhara poori thalis for Rs 11,072 — one of the largest vrat orders of the weekend.

Quick commerce told a similar story. Zepto Cafe served 12,500 portions of sabudana vada and falahari mixture during the festive period, BusinessLine reported, and demand for fasting ingredients rose sharply, with buckwheat flour orders up 16.4-fold and singhara flour up 16.1-fold compared with last year's Navratri period.

"The figures cover the period from October 17 to 20, when Navratri and Durga Puja celebrations culminated in Durga Ashtami, Maha Navami and Dussehra, Storyboard18 reported."

Rasgulla leads the sweet counter

Fasting was only half the plate. Orders for traditional sweets on Swiggy rose 36.4 percent between October 17 and 20 compared with a similar festive period last year. Rasgulla was the most-ordered sweet, averaging 495 orders an hour, led by Delhi, Mumbai and Gurugram. Gulab jamun, kaju katli, jalebi and rasmalai followed.

A Mumbai customer placed the period's largest rasgulla order — Rs 9,870 worth of assorted sweets including coffee rasgulla tiramisu. Demand was not confined to the largest metros: Bengaluru, Chennai, Delhi and Hyderabad led overall, while Patna, Dehradun, Jodhpur, Gaya and Thiruvananthapuram contributed significantly, and smaller towns including Agartala, Shillong, Palwal and Bathinda recorded notable sweet orders.

What the numbers show

Taken together, the data describe a festival eaten in two registers at once — strict vrat foods ordered by the thousand per hour during the fast, and celebratory sweets rising by more than a third as the festival closed. Delivery platforms, once a convenience for everyday meals, have become the route by which many households now source both the fasting plate and the festive box.

For readers outside India marking Navratri, the ordering pattern is a useful guide to the canonical vrat spread at home: sabudana khichdi and vada at the centre, singhara and rajgira pooris, kuttu and samak rice preparations, and makhana — followed, when the fast breaks, by rasgulla first.
